answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to a crystal cryptographic accumulator requiring verifiable stake burning. Creating n identities imposes a superlinear cost scaling as O(n^2) in burned collateral, ensuring an attacker cannot wander across forged nodes cheaply. Any disconnected cluster collapses into an isolated island without quorum validation, making coordinated adversarial takeover mathematically and economically unfeasible.
